chapter: Early influences, Oliver date and trombone peers
title: Coming into jazz: sneaking out at night and Jimmy Harrison
summary: He sneaked out of the dormitory to play for $5-10 a night; he claims no influences but went to hear trombonist Jimmy Harrison.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Who were some of your earliest influences. I mean, first of all, how did you get introduced to jazz?

Oh, my brother took me in the boarding school so ... I still had a horn and you had to stay on on Saturday night and you had to spend the night when you go in ... so I used to sneak out of the dormitory and go out and play at night and my brother would let me in. And then I got permission and we played quite a bit. And they played a lot of money, too.
What do you mean a lot of money, how much?
At the time about $5 or $10 a night was a lot of money, I'm telling you.
But, what made you decide to play jazz instead of playing poets or peasant or being...
I don't know. I just felt like playing jazz all of my life.
Well, what was one of the earliest trombonists that you listened to or trumpet player or somebody ...
I knew that was coming. I never had nobody to influence me, never.
Well, who were some of your favorites that you listened to in that period?

Jazz people, OWENS - Yeah, well, I didn't have no special people, I used to go listen to Jimmy Harrison. I said I was as good as they were. (... playing the horn ...) because practically every night, you know, that's when these places would stay open all night and we'd get through playing -- we'd play until 4 o'clock in the morning. Sometimes you'd play up until the next day ... sit back and drink your bottle, get high and blow your horn.
